match.reason: Neither bank point teaches the basic distinction between cash and credit transactions; one covers cash flow statement classification and the other covers cash flow management strategies, which are broader and different ideas.

draft.title: Cash and credit transactions
card: The money is paid or received at the time of the sale or purchase. Payment by EFTPOS, card or bank transfer on the spot counts as cash.
The goods or services are provided now, but payment is made later. No money changes hands on the day.
When a business sells on credit, the customer owes it money. This amount is an account receivable, and the business is owed it.
When a business buys on credit, it owes the supplier money. This amount is an account payable, and the business must pay it later.
draft.remember: Cash is paid at once. Credit is paid later, so someone owes someone.

a.q: Priya runs a bookkeeping service in Geelong. She finishes a job for a client today, and the client will pay in 30 days. What is this?
opts: A credit sale, so the client owes Priya money
A cash sale, so the client owes Priya money
A credit sale, so Priya owes the client money
A cash sale, so Priya has been paid in full
a.why: The service was given today but payment comes later, so it is a credit sale. Because the client has not yet paid, the client owes Priya, and the amount is an account receivable. It is not a cash sale, as no money was received today.
a.clue: Has any money been received today?

b.q: Tom's Mowing in Bendigo buys a new mower from a supplier today and agrees to pay in 14 days. Which describes Tom's Mowing now?
opts: It has an account payable to the supplier
It has an account receivable from the supplier
It has made a cash purchase from the supplier
It is owed money by the supplier until payment
b.why: Tom's Mowing got the mower now but has not paid, so it is a credit purchase. The business owes the supplier, which is an account payable. An account receivable is the reverse: money owed to the business by a customer.
b.clue: Who has to pay money later, Tom's Mowing or the supplier?

a.best: A credit sale, so the client owes Priya money

b.best: It has an account payable to the supplier
